title: F100 ANG Engine Exchange
description: The US Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC) F100 Program intends to issue a sole source �C�-type contract (named F100 Engine Exchange) to Pratt & Whitney (P&W), a Division of RTX Corporation for a �no-cost� exchange of property whereby the Government will deliver 51 F100-PW-220 engines to the Contractor, in exchange for the Contractor delivering 13 F100-229 new engine augmentor modules to the Government. A Sources Sought Synopsis (SSS) FA8124-RFI-AUG-2026 was posted from 4 August 2026 through 3 September 2026. Results from the SSS did not indicate any source other than P&W could perform the work under this contract at the prime level without the government incurring unacceptable delays and substantial duplication of costs not recoverable through competition. The government is awarding this contract under the authority of RFO 6.103-1,"Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements." A Justification and Approval (J&A) for using Other Than Full and Open Competition was approved on 23 October 2026. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement to the Contracting Officer by the date listed in this notice to be considered by the agency. Respondents shall specify status as a large business, small business, small disadvantaged business, 8(a) concern, women-owned small business, economically disadvantaged women-owned small business, HUBZone small business, veteran-owned small business, or service-disabled veteran-owned small business. This synopsis does not constitute an Invitation for Bids (IFB) or a Request for Proposals (RFP), nor does it restrict the Government to an ultimate acquisition approach. The government will not reimburse any costs associated with preparing or submitting a response to this notice. Due to security access requirements, foreign participation is not permitted at the prime contractor level. Contracting Activity: AFLCMC/LPK, 3001 Staff Dr, Tinker AFB, OK 73145.

title: C222--657A5-24-108, FCA Replace Medium Voltage Feeder 3 and Transformers l MC FY27 NRM VISN Base DE
description: Modification 2 to Presolicitation Notice 36C25527R0013 This modification provides answers to RFIs received and revised the evaluation criteria to be used for this project. RFIs Received for Project # 657A5-24-108, Replace Medium Voltage Feeder 3 and Transformers 1. Factor 4 Past Performance / Section F Project Eligibility � The solicitation states that projects submitted for past performance consideration must have completed both design and construction, and that projects not constructed will not be considered. Would the VA consider accepting relevant electrical infrastructure studies or assessments in Section F, particularly those involving medium-voltage distribution systems and feeder evaluations, that demonstrate directly applicable technical expertise but did not result in construction? We prefer to keep it as projects that were designed AND constructed.� Since this is a construction project and not a study, we want projects that have been finished to be used for past performance criteria. � 2. Factor 2 Specialized Experience and Technical Competence / Laboratory Requirements � Factor 2 references the firm's technical capabilities in design quality management procedures, CADD/BIM, equipment resources, and laboratory requirements. Given that the project scope primarily involves medium-voltage electrical feeder and transformer replacements, could the VA clarify the applicability of laboratory requirements to this project? We respectfully request that this criterion be removed from the evaluation requirements, as it does not appear directly relevant to the stated scope of work.� Laboratory requirements were deleted. Please see revised evaluation criteria below. � 3. Request for Submission Deadline Extension Given the technical scope of the project and the level of detail required to address the evaluation criteria, we respectfully request a one-week extension of the SF330 submission deadline, from November 10, 2026, to November 17, 2026. This additional time would allow interested firms to prepare comprehensive qualifications packages that fully address the solicitation requirements. SF330 submission due date extended from 11/10/2026 to 11/172026. End of RFIs.

title: FY27 HIOSH Hazardous Waste
description: Adding the Q&A and additional information. The purpose of this amendment 01 is to provide a revise RFQ with a revised SOW. The National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH) operates basic science research facilities in Cincinnati, Ohio; Morgantown, West Virginia; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania; and Spokane, Washington. Each location generates hazardous, universal, and other regulated waste through research and laboratory operations. Each location is considered a Small Quantity Generator of hazardous waste. The approximate average monthly quantities generated are: Location Approximate Monthly Quantity Cincinnati, Ohio 100 pounds Morgantown, West Virginia 500 pounds Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania 150 pounds Spokane, Washington 50 pounds Each location shall be treated as a separate job site. Hazardous waste shall be collected quarterly from designated collection areas. Contractor personnel shall not be required to enter individual laboratories. The acquisition is being pursued to obtain compliant collection, packaging, transportation, documentation, treatment, and final disposal services for waste generated at NIOSH facilities. The contractor shall provide complete cradle-to-final-disposal services and maintain the documentation necessary to demonstrate proper management of each waste stream. Performance shall comply with all applicable Federal, state, and local laws and regulations, including, as applicable, the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act, the Toxic Substances Control Act, the Occupational Safety and Health Act, the Hazardous Materials Transportation Act, applicable United States Department of Transportation regulations in 49 CFR Parts 100�199, and applicable requirements in 40 CFR Parts 261 and 264/265. PURPOSE/OBJECTIVE The purpose of this acquisition is to obtain safe, lawful, and fully documented management of hazardous, universal, and other regulated waste generated at four NIOSH research facilities. The contractor shall provide all personnel, labor, supervision, transportation, packaging, equipment, supplies, supplies, permits, licenses, analysis, documentation, and other resources necessary to: Collect waste from designated collection areas; Package and label waste for shipment; Prepare and process required manifests and shipping documents; Transport waste in compliance with applicable requirements; Determine appropriate treatment or disposal methods; Ensure waste is delivered to properly permitted facilities; Complete final treatment or final disposal; and Provide documentation and audit trails demonstrating the ultimate disposition of each waste item. The contractor shall perform all work in a safe, prudent, conscientious, and professional manner. Work shall be performed during NIOSH normal working hours and shall comply with all applicable safety, environmental, transportation, and security requirements. SCOPE OF WORK The contractor shall provide quarterly removal of listed waste streams for the Cincinnati, Morgantown, Pittsburgh, and Spokane NIOSH locations. Each site shall be considered a separate job for scheduling, pickup, invoicing, documentation, and performance purposes. The contractor shall not be required to enter individual laboratories. All hazardous chemicals waste, universal waste, additional waste listed below, and gas cylinders are not associated with all four sites. Waste may include the following: Hazardous chemical waste Flammable liquids, including alcohol, xylene, acetonitrile, and ethyl acetate; Non-pouring flammables, including gas cylinders, solids, and metal powders; Inorganic and organic acids; Inorganic and organic bases; Oxidizers; Solid metals and metal powders; U-listed and P-listed wastes; Peroxides and reactive waste; Mercury compounds; Non-RCRA solids and liquids; Dioxin; Pentachlorophenol and polychlorinated biphenyl waste; Flammable aerosols; Formaldehyde, formaldehyde solutions, and glutaraldehyde-containing tissue specimens; Small quantities of explosives, generally from 1 to 1,000 grams; Paints; Sodium cacodylate; Potassium cacodylate; Waste oil; and Used or expired self-contained self-rescuer cartridges. Universal waste Batteries; Pesticides; Mercury-containing equipment; Lamps; and Aerosol cans. Additional waste Used oils; Charcoal filters; and Aqueous waste. Gas cylinders Toxic, corrosive, flammable, oxidizing, or refrigerant gas cylinders; Majority of cylinders are high pressure steel, 9-10�D X 48-51�H Some cylinders in Pittsburgh have unidentified contents. Gas-cylinder removal shall be provided as a separate line item. The estimated quantities are: Location Estimated Cylinders Cincinnati, Ohio 0 Morgantown, West Virginia 10 Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania 75 Spokane, Washington 15 Gas cylinders may be removed in one service event or over the life of the contract. Once removed, the cylinders are not expected to be replaced. The contractor shall provide lab-packs, drums, overpacks, packaging materials, labels, and other equipment necessary to safely consolidate, package, transport, and dispose of the waste. The contractor shall remain responsible for proper management of waste after it leaves NIOSH property, including transportation, spills, leaks, treatment, final disposal, and supporting documentation. TASKS TO BE PERFORMED Task 1: Provide Waste Collection and Packaging Services The contractor shall schedule and perform quarterly waste pickups at each NIOSH location. a. The contractor shall coordinate pickup dates with the designated NIOSH representative. b. The contractor shall collect waste from designated collection areas. c. The contractor shall not require access to individual laboratories. d. The contractor shall treat each NIOSH location as a separate job for scheduling and invoicing. The contractor shall provide all packaging and handling services required for safe shipment. a. The contractor shall supply lab-packs, drums, overpacks, labels, containers, absorbent materials, and other necessary packaging. b. The contractor shall package waste in accordance with applicable requirements. c. The contractor shall not require separation of tissue from formaldehyde solutions containing tissue. d. The contractor shall identify and manage incompatible waste streams appropriately. The contractor shall provide a separate line item for gas-cylinder removal. a. The contractor shall remove gas cylinders identified by NIOSH. b. The contractor shall manage cylinders with known or unidentified contents in accordance with applicable requirements. c. The contractor may remove cylinders during one service event or over the life of the contract. Task 2: Provide Transportation, Treatment, and Final Disposal Services The contractor shall transport waste in accordance with all applicable requirements. a. The contractor shall comply with United States Department of Transportation requirements in 49 CFR Parts 100�199. b. The contractor shall ensure that all approved subcontractors and transporters comply with applicable transportation requirements. c. The contractor shall ensure that shipping papers include required technical names, emergency-response information, and a 24-hour emergency telephone number. d. The contractor shall ensure that off-site shipments are properly labeled, marked, and placarded. The contractor shall provide final treatment and final disposal of all waste. a. The contractor shall send waste only to licensed, permitted, and approved facilities. b. The contractor shall ensure that each facility is authorized to handle the applicable waste streams and RCRA waste codes. c. Mere acceptance of waste at a treatment, storage, or disposal facility shall not constitute final treatment or final disposal. d. The contractor shall obtain documentation demonstrating completion of final treatment or final disposal. title: MACH1_AOI_Military Working Dog Facility_ Vandenberg Space Force_LOE 1 and LOE 2
description: This Area of Interest (AOI) is published under the Modernized Agile Construction Horizons (MACH1) Umbrella Program Notice. All submissions must adhere to the procedures and guidelines outlined in the parent MACH1 framework document unless otherwise tailored herein. Any resulting agreement will be an Other Transaction Agreement (OTA) executed under the statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. The 772nd Enterprise Sourcing Squadron (772 ESS) is is executing a Progressive Design-Build (PDB) project to renovate existing military working dog (MWD) facilities and construct a new addition at Vandenberg Space Force Base (SFB), California. Under this agreement, the selected contractor will execute both the progressive design and physical construction to deliver a fully functional, code-compliant compound (Project Number: XUMU171121C). The current MWD kennel and admin facilities (Buildings 6444 and 6447) at Vandenberg SFB fail quarterly inspections and contain critical safety hazards that endanger military personnel and canine assets. Transitioning to a Progressive Design-Build (PDB) model is critical to eliminate traditional design-bid-build delays, rapidly deliver compliant spaces, and preserve the security mission of the 30th Space Wing. There are (2) two distinct lines of effort (LOEs) for this requirement: LOE 1 - Design & Planning (Design) and LOE 2 - Physical Construction. See attachment PDF: MACH1_AOI_FA890327OT005_Military_Working_Dog_Facility_Vandenberg_ 20 Oct 26.pdf

description: The Army Contracting Command � Rock Island (ACC-RI) is issuing this sources sought synopsis as a means of conducting market research to identify potential sources having an interest to provide Versamid V-140 material to Crane Army Ammunition Activity, Crane, Indiana. The result of this market research will contribute to determining this method of procurement, if a requirement materializes. Based on the response to this sources sought notice/ market research, this requirement may be set-aside for small business (in full or in part) or procured through full and open competition. All small business set-aside categories will be considered. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged, and no feedback or evaluations will be provided to companies regarding submissions. PRODUCT SPECIFICATION Versamid V-140 is used in the composition for all 60mm, 81mm, 120mm and 155mm VL candles. The contractor shall deliver Versamid V-140 material that strictly conforms to the following physical and performance specifications: The material must exhibit an Amine Value of 350 to 400 mg KOH/gram resin, a Specific Gravity of approximately 0.97 at 25 degrees Celsius, and a maximum Gardner Color rating of 12. Furthermore, the material must maintain a Viscosity of 80 to 140 poise at 25 degrees Celsius. Upon physical delivery, all furnished material must have a minimum of eighty percent (80%) of its original shelf-life remaining to be accepted. A minimum of 220 Gallons per contract is required. A maximum of 5500 Gallons per contract. A FAT Quantity of 1 Gallon may be required. DISCLAIMER This sources sought is for information purposes only. This is NOT a Request for Proposal/ Quotation (RFP/ RFQ) to be submitted. It does not constitute a solicitation and shall not be construed as a commitment by the government. Responses in any form are not offers and the government is under NO obligation to award a contract as a result of this announcement. No funds are available to pay for preparation of responses to this announcement. Any information submitted by respondents to this technical description is strictly voluntary. Wideband and Narrowband Global SATCOM Sustainment (WNGSS) IDIQ Contract
description: The United States Space Force (USSF), Space Systems Command (SSC), intends to award a sole-source Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract to The Boeing Company (CAGE: 18600), P.O. Box 92919, Los Angeles, CA 90009-2919, for the Wideband and Narrowband Global SATCOM Sustainment (WNGSS) effort. The anticipated contract will have a five-year base ordering period and one ten-year optional ordering period, with a total estimated ceiling of approximately $945.9M ($480.6M base and $465.3M option) if all options are exercised. This IDIQ contract will provide the critical, full life-cycle engineering, sustainment, cybersecurity, modernization, and operational enhancement support for multiple Military Satellite Communications (MILSATCOM) constellations. The scope of this requirement includes, but is not limited to: Space Vehicle & Constellation Sustainment: 24/7 real-time anomaly analysis, fault isolation, and recovery; factory reachback engineering; telemetry trending; orbital analysis; maneuver planning; collision avoidance (COLA); and end-of-life (EOL) disposal for the Wideband Global SATCOM (WGS) and Ultra High Frequency Follow-On (UFO) satellite constellations. Ground Command & Control Support: Sustaining engineering, software maintenance, and enhancement for the Global SATCOM Configuration and Control Element (GSCCE) ground system. Software, Database, & Simulation Sustainment: Maintenance and updates for satellite flight software, the Satellite Simulator (SATSIM), operational databases, and engineering tools. Pre-Handover & Transition Support: Support for the transition of new space vehicles (e.g., WGS-11, WGS-12) and hosted payloads (e.g., Protected Tactical SATCOM Prototype [PTS-P]) from development into the operational sustainment baseline. Statutory Authority: This acquisition is being conducted on a sole-source basis under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 6.302-1, "Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements." Justification for Sole Source: The Boeing Company is the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) for the WGS satellites, UFO satellites, and critical components of the GSCCE ground system. Boeing possesses unique qualifications and exclusive ownership of the proprietary data, software, and specialized infrastructure required to perform this sustainment effort. The Government does not possess sufficient data license rights for the technical data packages (TDPs), flight software source code, or high-fidelity satellite simulators (SATSIM) to permit a competitive acquisition. This proprietary data, which was developed at private expense, includes detailed design documentation for the Boeing 702HP and 702MP satellite platforms, simulators, and ground control software. Boeing has repeatedly declined the Government�s requests to sell the necessary data rights. Without access to this OEM-owned data, no other contractor can perform the required engineering and sustainment without introducing substantial duplication of cost to the Government and unacceptable delays and risk to on-orbit assets critical to national security. Market research confirmed that Boeing is the only contractor fully capable of satisfying all of the requirements of this acquisition without a break in critical service to the warfighter.

Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. Submission: Agency protests should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. title: GA-VGMS-33528
description: This is a request for information (RFI) / SOURCES SOUGHT SYNOPSIS. This request is not a solicitation (Request for Proposal or Request for Quotations) or a promise to issue a solicitation in the future. Responses to this notice are not considered offers and cannot be accepted by the government to form a binding contract. The purpose of this request for information is in support of market research being conducted by the Air Force Metrology Calibration Program (AFMETCAL) to identify potential sources and gather information on current capabilities within the market. This synopsis is for planning purposes only and is NOT to be construed as a commitment by the Government nor will the Government pay for information solicited hereunder. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the responding party's expense. The level of security clearance and amount of foreign participation in this requirement has not been determined. All information received in response to this RFI that is marked PROPRIETARY will be handled accordingly. Proprietary information will be safeguarded in accordance with the applicable Government regulations. Proprietary information or trade secrets should be clearly identified. If, after reviewing these documents, you desire to participate in the market research, you should provide documentation that supports your company's capability in meeting these requirements. Failure to provide documentation may result in the government being unable to adequately assess your capabilities. If you lack sufficient experience in a particular area, please provide details explaining how you would overcome the lack of experience/capabilities in order to perform that portion of the requirement (i.e., teaming, subcontracting, etc.) Both large and small businesses are encouraged to participate in this Market Research. Joint ventures or teaming arrangements are encouraged. Currently there are no funds available for this acquisition. The Air Force Metrology & Calibration (AFMETCAL) program office is seeking sources capable of providing an upgrade to a primary vacuum standard. Work includes integrating additional hardware to the system, updating the proprietary software, and verifying performance of upgrade onsite to allow calibration of analog output vacuum gauges. Work includes correction of various issues with software bugs. Interested vendors should submit a brief capability statement including company information (DUNS, CAGE, business size), relevant experience, and rough order of magnitude pricing. The NAICS code assigned to this acquisition is 334515 with a size standard of 750 employees. The total estimated quantity of 1 unit over 1 year. Reconditioned, remanufactured, or used material is not acceptable for this item. Offerors responding to this sources sought market research notice must: (1) state whether you are a small or large business, if you are the manufacturer or provide the name of the manufacturer and size info of product you would be offering and the socioeconomic status and indicate small disadvantaged or woman-owned business, veteran owned, service disabled veteran owned, 8(a) historically black college or university or minority institution (HBCU/MI), or a historically underutilized business zone (HUBZone) (2) provide sales history including recent sales to commercial companies (3) advise if your product is a commercial item or if it will be modified; if not commercial at this time, will you be offering this item to the general public in the future. (4) advise if you have the item on a GSA schedule or other Government contract include front page of schedule and the page showing the part is on award (5) provide information concerning the technical capabilities of the product you are interested in offering, including commercial literature/brochures and warranty. Include any other pertinent information which would enable the government to assess your firm�s capabilities (6) advise if you accept the Government purchase card (7) Provide Point of Contact including: company/ institute name, address, phone number and email address (8) provide assigned Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) Code (9) Verify if your company/institute is listed in the System for Award Management (SAM) (10) State if your company is domestically or foreign owned (if foreign owned, please indicate the country of ownership) (11) Advise how much time you would need to submit a technical proposal if a solicitation is issued (12) provide an estimated price for one each, an estimated price for the total quantity and provide any price quantity discounts based on the total estimated quantity (13) include estimated delivery time for shipment. Ensure only .pdf, .doc or .xls documents are attached to your email. Submit all responses to the listed point of contact. If an email response is not possible, submit by FAX to 937-713-5841 or mail to 813 Irving-wick Dr W., Horton Building, Heath OH 43056-1199. Reference 27M-638A-VA in all correspondence. Responses are due by 11/17/2026 at 2:00pm ET or 1400 hours; however, early responses are encouraged. description: This is not a solicitation announcement. This is a Sources Sought Notice (SSN) only. This SSN is issued solely for market research and planning purposes � it does not constitute a Request for Quotation (RFQ) or a promise to issue an RFQ in the future. Further, the SSN does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. The FDA is not seeking proposals and will not accept any unsolicited proposals. Responders are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this SSN; all costs associated with responding to this SSN will be solely at the expense of the interested respondents. Not responding to this SSN does not preclude participation in any future RFQ, if issued. The purpose of this SSN is to gain knowledge of potential qualified vendors, including large business sources, small business sources and their size classifications (i.e., HUBZone 8(a), 8(a), HUBZone, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned, Veteran-Owned, Women-Owned Small Business, and Small Disadvantaged Business) relative to the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code. Responses to this SSN will be used by the Government to make appropriate determinations about potential sources. Project Title: FDA/CDRH Scientific Technical Capacity for Regulatory Review Background: To assist the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Center for Devices and Radiological Health (CDRH) in fulfilling its mission, CDRH seeks expert consultants to assist CDRH�s Offices with regulatory review across the total product lifecycle. CDRH requires consultants that have skilled experience to assist with medical device regulatory review work and supporting scientific activities, such as research, cybersecurity and digital health consultations, regulatory consultations and auditing, and interacting with industry and patients. The CDRH requires consultants that have sufficient skilled capacity in many science, engineering, and clinical specialties, including Anesthesiology, Biology, Biomedical Engineering, Chemistry, Clinical laboratory testing, Computer Science and Engineering, Consumer Safety, Cybersecurity, Data Science, Dentistry, Digital Health, Epidemiology, Gastroenterology, General Engineering, Health Science, Infectious Diseases, Interdisciplinary Engineer/Scientist, Molecular testing, Neurology, Optics, Patient Engagement, Physics, Psychiatry, Public Health, Pulmonology, Reprocessing medical devices, Social Scientist, Software Engineering, Statistics and Biostatistics, Sterilization, Toxicology, Urology, Veterinary Medicine, and Virology. Objective: The primary objective of this effort is to provide the CDRH with a vehicle to acquire the support services of advanced professional and scientific consultants to assist CDRH�s Offices with regulatory review across the total product lifecycle, including the supporting scientific, engineering, clinical, and regulatory activities. The services provided will be critical scientific expertise and capacity in support for the evaluation of the continued performance, safety, and effectiveness, with respect to devices approved, cleared, licensed, or authorized for use for the treatment, prevention, or diagnosis of medical conditions by the FDA. Instructions for Responses to this SSN: Your responses to the questions provided below will assist the Government in selecting the appropriate acquisition method. Page limit: Maximum 15 pages (font size Times New Roman 11 or larger). In addition to responses to the below questions, each vendor responding to this SSN shall also fill out and provide responses to �Attachment B-Vendor Feedback Form.� The Vendor Feedback Form is not included in the 15-page limit. A copy of the company capability statement will also be accepted (but not in place of the responses to the below questions or the Vendor Feedback Form). The anticipated period of performance consists of one (1) Base Year and four (4) Option Years. Responses to this SSN must include company name, address, point of contact, size of business pursuant to the NAICS code, and must respond to the following questions: Is your business a small business under the NAICS code? Does your firm qualify as a Small Disadvantaged Business? If disadvantaged, specify if your firm is certified under Section 8(a) of the Small Business Act? Are you considered a certified HUBZone firm? Are you considered Woman-Owned or operated business? Are you a certified Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned or Veteran-Owned business? Included is a draft Statement of Work that is inclusive of the anticipated Task Areas (�Attachment A-Draft Statement of Work�). All interested parties can provide written opinions/questions on the draft Statement of Work. All opinions/questions expressed should focus on strengthening the draft Statement of Work Tasks to ensure industry understands and comprehends the government�s requirements. Responses to this SSN shall be submitted via e-mail to Melinda Kim, Contract Specialist, at Melinda.Kim@fda.hhs.gov, (with a CC: to Nicholas Bisher, Contracting Officer, at Nicholas.Bisher@fda.hhs.gov), by 2:00 PM Eastern Standard Time on November 17, 2026. The subject line of the e-mail shall reference, �Vendor Response to SSN 75F40127Q00006.� After a review of the received responses, a formal solicitation may be published on SAM.gov or on GSA eBuy. No solicitation is currently available. This is not a request for quotation and in no way obligates the Government to award any contract. Responses to this SSN will not be considered adequate responses to the solicitation, a request to be added to a prospective offerors list, or a request to receive a copy of the solicitation. title: Acadia National Park
description: Sealed bids from certified Small Business Concerns only will be accepted for Acadia National Park, Project ME NP ACAD BRG(2), Solicitation Number 693C73-27-B-000002, located in Hancock County, Maine. The project consists of repair of Main Route 233, Paradise Hill, and Frazer Creek Bridges. The work includes reconstruction of asphalt concrete pavement and aggregate base course, placement of structural backfill, cleaning and removing debris from weepholes and inlets, cleaning and sealing joints, erosion repair, repointing mortar joints, placing waterproofing membrane to improve the service life, and other miscellaneous work. The project will be split into multiple work schedules/contract options, with the cost of the entire project expected to fall within the price range of $2,000,000 to $3,000,000. Bid documents should be issued on or about October 9, 2026. Bid due date and location will be specified on the SF 1442, Block 13a of the Solicitation. Use Internet address https://www.sam.gov (click on Contract Opportunities, then type �693C73� in the Search Contract Opportunities box and click the search button and all available projects will be listed) to check for the availability of advertisement documents. All documents can be directly downloaded from this website. Solicitation documents will not be mailed. Register to receive email notifications to be automatically notified when a document is added or updated for a specific project. If firms do not register as an interested vendor at this website, there will be no Interested Vendors List. Please send all questions concerning construction projects to eflhd.contracts@dot.gov. Include the solicitation number, project name and number, requesting firm and address, a point of contact and telephone number. Requests for 'faxing' or overnight mailing will not be accepted. IMPORTANT SAM REGISTRATION AND PAYMENT REQUIREMENTS In accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 52.204-7 (DEVIATION NOV 2025), prospective contractors shall have an active Federal Government contracts registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) when submitting an offer in response to this solicitation and at the time of award. To register in SAM, go to https://www.sam.gov. Annual contractor representations and certifications must be completed online at https://www.sam.gov. Also, FAR 52.232-33 requires SAM registration for payment. The required annual Form VETS-4212 must also be completed online at http://www.dol.gov/vets/vets4212.htm per FAR 52.222-37. PLEASE NOTE For security reasons, individuals requiring access to all government buildings must present a valid photo ID and be escorted to their destination by a Government employee. All visitors attending bid openings are urged to arrive at least 1 hour prior to a scheduled bid opening. All visitors must sign in at the main entrance of the Quantum Park facility and wait to be escorted by a Government employee to Eastern Federal Lands Highway Division (EFLHD) in Suite 200. Visitors must then register with the EFLHD Receptionist. A Government employee will collect all bids. Prior to the bid opening, a Government employee will escort all bidders to the bid opening. Unescorted visitors will be denied entry and no exceptions will be made. Bidders are encouraged to submit bids electronically per the instructions provided in the solicitation.

description: The Air Force Services Center (AFSVC), headquartered at Joint Base San Antonio- Lackland, Texas, delivers Services programs and activities to build and sustain ready and resilient Airmen, Guardians and families. Air Force Services Center supports the bases, major commands and air staff by providing technical assistance, new initiatives, developing programs and procedures and managing central support functions. Air Force Services Center ensures successful operation of essential food, fitness, childcare, lodging and recreation opportunities for military members and their families. The Center�s responsibilities include preparing responses to high-level inquiries, providing technical assistance to the field and developing new programs that support major command and installation activities. The Financial Management Directorate (VF) manages the Nonappropriated Fund Public Accountant Contract Audit program centrally which supports a worldwide mission providing an oversight of internal controls, cash management and financial information to installations at the enterprise level. Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) installations provide support services and activities for military personnel, families and authorized patrons. Proper management and accountability of Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) resources are critical to ensuring continued service delivery and the protection of government interests. Regular audits are required to evaluate the financial status, internal controls, and operational effectiveness of Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) operations. The Air Force Services Center Financial Management, Strategic Policy & Financial Operations, AFSVC/VFSF manages and administers audit oversight to Central Funds and the Public Accountant Contract Audit (PACA) Program to ensure compliance with annual audit requirements of financial statements audits of the NAFIs and that adequate audit coverage is provided Air Force wide for the Nonappropriated Fund Instrumentalities (NAFIs) Services activities. The Contractor shall conduct comprehensive audits of the financial statements, transactions, internal controls, and performance of Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) installations and activities. AFSVC is seeking to contract an audit firm for a 5-year period, structured with a Base Year and four (4) subsequent Option Years. AFSVC intends to issue initial Base Year task orders requiring dual-year financial statement audits encompassing two distinct historical fiscal years as designated in the individual task orders (e.g., FY24 and FY25). While financial statement audits will examine specific, historical fiscal years, performance audits will be conducted on an as-needed basis determined by an annual risk assessment, with the specific scope defined in individual task orders

title: Sources Sought for HOBAS pipe (centrifugally cast fiberglass-reinforced polymer mortar)
description: The Government intends to procure, under only one responsible source, where no other suppliers or service will satisfy the agency requirements. The Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command, Hawaii (NAVFAC Hawaii) is conducting market research to determine if other potential products/services can provide for a centrifugally cast fiberglass-reinforced polymer mortar (CCFRPM) pipe that has the equal performance and listing/approval requirements as the HOBAS pipe (CCFRPM pipe), manufactured by HOBAS Pipe USA, Inc., 1413 E. Richey Road, Houston, Texas 77073-3508. The alternate product/service must meet the following requirements and specifications: Centrifugally cast fiberglass-reinforced polymer (CCFRPM) pipe, manufactured and tested in accordance with ASTM D3262. Pipe sizes shall be 24-inch (DN 600, 25.8-inch OD) and 42-inch (DN 1050, 45.9-inch OD) nominal diameters. Manufactured by the centrifugal casting process to result in a dense, uniform, non-porous, corrosion-resistant, consistent composite structure. Interior surface of the pipe exposed to untreated sewer flow must provide crack and abrasion resistance. Exterior surface of the pipe must be comprised of a sand and resin layer that provides ultraviolet (UV) protection to the pipe exterior. Pipes must be Type 1, Liner 2, Grade 3 per ASTM D3262. Coupling joints must meet the requirements of ASTM D4161. Minimum pipe normal stiffness (SN) when tested in accordance with ASTM D2412 must be 46 pound per square inch (PSI). Resin System: Manufacturer must use only polyester resin systems with proven history of performance in this application. Historical data must be acquired from a composite material or similar construction and composition as the proposed product. Glass Reinforcement: The reinforcing glass fibers used to manufacture the components must be of the highest quality commercial grade E-glass filaments with binder and sizing compatible with impregnating resins. Silica Sand: Sand must be minimum 98% silica with a maximum moisture content of 0.2%. Additives: Resin additives, such as curing agents, pigments, dyes, fillers, and thixotropic agents, etc., when used, must not detrimentally affect the performance of the product. Elastomeric Gaskets: Gaskets must meet ASTM F477 and be suitable for the intended service. This notification is for market research purposes only and should not be construed as a commitment of any kind by the U.S. Government to issue a solicitation, request for proposals, quotes, or invitation of bids or award a contract. Interested parties with a comparable product meeting the requirements described in this announcement are invited to submit complete technical data, information and specifications in order for the Government to conduct an evaluation of your product to ensure compatibility with the existing system. Technical response shall be typed, at least 11 point Times New Roman or larger, single-sided 8.5 by 11 inch pages and submitted in Adobe PDF format. Also, provide company information and point of contract (name, title, email, phone, mailing address). The Government will not reimburse any responder for any costs associated with information submitted in response to this sources sought announcement. Any information provided to the Government in response to this request for information (RFI) will become U.S. Government property and will not be returned. All proprietary or classified information will be treated appropriately. The Government reserves the right to disregard any submittal that is incomplete or vague. Please do not submit your company brochure. Interested parties shall submit information and specifications to Ms. Isabella Chong-Navarre, Contract Specialist via email at isabella.a.chong-navarre.civ@us.navy.mil and Ms. Jessica Shimoda, Contract Specialist via email at Jessica.a.shimoda.civ@us.navy.mil. Interested parties responding to this announcement by 17, November 2026 at 10:00 A.M. Hawaii Standard Time will be considered.

title: 3 MXS Vertical Tank System (VTS) Removal -Re-Solicitation
description: Restriction of Competition to Original Interested Parties (Solicitation FA500026Q0075) Classification Code: J039 � Maint, Repair, Rebuild of Equipment - Miscellaneous NAICS Code: 562119 � Other Waste Collection (Size Standard: $47.0M) Contracting Activity: Department of the Air Force, Pacific Air Forces (PACAF), 673d Contracting Squadron (673 CONS/PKB), Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson (JBER), AK 99506-2501 Original Solicitation Number: FA500026Q0075 (Posted: 12 October 2026 on SAM.gov) Associated Terminated Contract: FA500026P0092 Governing Directives / Attachments: Stop-Work Order Notice (Directive FA500026P0092_RFO_Corrected; Effective 27 October 2026 / Acknowledged 3 November 2026) Incumbent / Terminated Vendor: International Automated Systems (IAS), PO Box 56, Baldwin, WI 54002-0056 (POC: Andrea Jeszewski) Anticipated Replacement Solicitation: FA500026Q0075-R (or as designated by the Contracting Officer) Notice Type: Special Notice / Notice of Intent to Limit Competition to Original Offerors Primary Point of Contact: Daniel P. Swoyer, Contracting Officer 673 CONS/PKB, 10480 Sijan Ave, Suite 242, JBER, AK 99506-2501 Email: daniel.swoyer.1@us.af.mil | Phone: (907) 552-5587 1. GENERAL INFORMATION & PURPOSE The 673d Contracting Squadron (673 CONS/PKB), Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson (JBER), Alaska, hereby issues this Notice of Intent to announce the Government�s intent to re-solicit the requirement for the Disassembly, Removal, and Disposal of the External Aircraft Fuel Tank Storage System (EAFTSS) / Vertical Tank Storage (VTS) by limiting competition exclusively to those responsible offerors who previously submitted timely quotations and were deemed interested parties under Solicitation FA500026Q0075. This notice is published in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (RFO) part 5, FAR 5.301, and Comptroller General / Government Accountability Office (GAO) appropriations and procurement case law governing replacement contracts following a termination for convenience. 2. BACKGROUND & REASON FOR RE-SOLICITATION Award and Identification of Government Error in PWS: Following competition under Solicitation FA500026Q0075, the Government awarded purchase order FA500026P0092 to International Automated Systems, Inc. (IAS) in the amount of $60,638.00. Subsequent to award, the Government identified a material drafting error in Section 1.3 of the Performance Work Statement (PWS). The PWS erroneously described the requirement as removing a total of 100 positions (Model V-100-2, 2 lines, 100 positions per line). The actual physical requirement of the 3d Maintenance Squadron (3 MXS) / 525th Aircraft Maintenance Unit (AMU) requires the disassembly, removal, and Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) disposition of four (4) VTS carousel systems with 50 positions each, for a true total of 200 positions across Buildings 10555 and 10565. Issuance and Execution of Stop-Work Order (RFO Directive): Upon discovery of the defective specification, Contracting Officer Daniel P. Swoyer issued a formal Stop-Work Order Notice (Stop_Work_Order_FA500026P0092_RFO_Corrected) dated 27 October 2026 pursuant to contract authority RFO 52.212-4 / FAR 52.212-4. In accordance with the directive: The Contractor (IAS, POC: Andrea Jeszewski) was directed to immediately halt all operational, administrative, and technical performance, minimize costs, and flow down the stoppage to all subcontractors and suppliers. IAS formally signed and returned the Acknowledgment of Receipt effective 3 November 2026. Under Section 5 of the RFO directive, any work performed on or after 3 November 2026 without Contracting Officer authorization was established as unauthorized and non-reimbursable. No-Cost Termination for Convenience: Following consultation regarding the 90-day stoppage period and potential equitable adjustment rights under RFO 52.212-4, Contracting Officer Daniel P. Swoyer requested a complete, no-cost termination for the convenience of the Government. IAS formally agreed to the no-cost settlement, waiving all termination settlement costs and equitable adjustments. Contract FA500026P0092 was completely terminated, and all obligated funds ($60,638.00) were scheduled for de-obligation. Necessity of Replacement Acquisition: Doubling the physical scope from 100 positions to 200 positions represents a cardinal change outside the scope of the original competition. Amending the terminated contract would violate the Competition in Contracting Act (CICA). Consequently, a replacement solicitation with the corrected PWS must be conducted. 3. LEGAL & REGULATORY BASIS FOR RESTRICTING RE-SOLICITATION The Government intends to restrict the replacement solicitation exclusively to the pool of vendors who participated as interested offerors under FA500026Q0075 pursuant to the GAO Replacement Contract Doctrine (see Delta Ventures, B-238655; Computervision Corp., B-237446; and 70 Comp. Gen. 230): Substantial Similarity of Requirement: The physical nature of the work�disassembly, electrical/mechanical disconnect, extraction without structural facility alteration, and DLA disposition of IAS-manufactured VTS carousels�remains identical in technical character to the original solicitation, with the sole modification being the correction of unit quantity from 100 to 200 positions. Preservation of the Original Competition: Full and open competition (100% Small Business Set-Aside) was conducted on SAM.gov under FA500026Q0075. The original competitive field demonstrated technical capability, pricing methodologies, and readiness to mobilize to JBER. Limiting the re-solicitation to these qualified firms preserves the integrity of the original competitive effort without affording an unfair advantage. Mission Expediency and Facility Readiness: The four (4) inactive VTS carousels occupy critical floor space in Buildings 10555 and 10565 required for active 3d Wing aircraft maintenance operations. Re-competing across the open market would introduce substantial delays contrary to mission requirements. 4. DESCRIPTION OF CORRECTED WORK SCOPE The replacement solicitation will incorporate the corrected PWS reflecting the following validated parameters: Equipment Identification: External Aircraft Fuel Tank Storage System (EAFTSS) / Vertical Tank Storage (VTS) Carousels manufactured by International Automated Systems (IAS). Corrected Scope of Work: Complete mechanical and electrical disassembly, removal, and turn-in/disposal of four (4) VTS Carousels, each configured with 50 storage positions, for an overall total of 200 positions. Work Location: 525 AMU, 11540 Slammer Avenue (Buildings 10555 and 10565), Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson (JBER), AK 99506-2701. Operational Constraints: Work must be executed inside the facility without structural facility modifications. The contractor is responsible for all rigging, certified technician labor, safety oversight, hazardous material handling, and transport to DLA Disposition Services. 5. NOTICE TO INDUSTRY & SUBMISSION OF CAPABILITY STATEMENTS THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES. It is a notice of intent to issue a restricted replacement solicitation to the offerors who responded to Solicitation FA500026Q0075. However, in accordance with FAR 5.207, any responsible vendor�other than those who submitted offers under FA500026Q0075�that believes it possesses the specialized technical capability, manufacturer-compliant tooling, certified personnel (electrical/mechanical), and logistical capacity to mobilize to JBER, Alaska and execute the removal of 200 VTS positions within the required timeframe may submit a written capability statement. Submission Criteria: Deadline for Response: Responses must be received no later than seven (7) calendar days from the posting date of this notice, at 14:00 Alaska Standard Time (AKST). Submission Format: Electronic submission via email to the Contracting Officer at daniel.swoyer.1@us.af.mil in searchable Adobe PDF format (maximum 5 pages). Required

title: Multi-Mission Commercial Launch Services (MCLS) Request for Information
description: Description NASA�s Commercial Access to Space Program and Launch Services Program Office (LSP) are seeking statements of interest from industry demonstrating the interest, experience, and capability to provide launch services in support of the Multi-Mission Commercial Launch Services (MCLS) requirements identified below. General Project Requirements NASA intends to procure launch services through a full and open competition for at least eight (8) full-mission-assurance launches to the following orbits: Two (2) High C3 Orbit in 2031 Two (2) Lagrange/Lunar Orbit in 2030 Three (3) Sun Synchronous Orbit (SSO) in 2030 (2 mission) and 2031 (1 mission) One (1) Low Earth Orbit (LEO) in 2030 These missions will require full NASA insight and full mission assurance; however, they will not require a completed first flight prior to proposal receipt. Full mission assurance is described as a Contractor providing NASA an adequate level of insight into and/or approval of certain Contractor tasks and milestones in order to ensure all reasonable steps have been taken that result in the highest probability of mission success. These requirements are subject to change. Request for Information Goals and Objectives The goal of this RFI is to improve both NASA's understanding of industry capabilities and the industry's understanding of NASA's needs by collecting industry feedback on the planned procurement process and evaluation strategy for the MCLS acquisition. This information will help LSP understand how to best structure the upcoming solicitation and evaluation criteria to align with industry�s best practices and maximize competition. Please complete the attached questionnaire detailing your perspectives on the most effective procurement approach. Industry Day: NASA LSP intends to host a virtual forum with industry (i.e., �Industry Day�) on the 12th and 13th of November 2026 to engage in open discussion and dialogue to answer questions interested parties may have regarding the NASA�s contemplated MCLS acquisition strategy. The objective of this event is to receive industry�s feedback on the MCLS acquisition strategy and provide industry with additional details about the MCLS acquisition. Additionally, if there are any procurement topics you recommend LSP specifically address at Industry Day, please let us know by 10 November 2026. Finally, please indicate if you would like to discuss any topic(s) individually. Immediately following Industry Day, LSP will offer sixty (60)-minute timeslots for one-on-one meetings with each interested party. Timing of these one-on-one meetings is tentative and will depend on the number of RSVPs received, timing of the Industry Day, etc. Those who wish to attend are encouraged to RSVP to the virtual Industry Day and one-on-one meetings as soon as possible, but no later than 9 November 2026, 3:00PM EST. The purpose of this RFI and upcoming Industry Day is to conduct market research for currently available launch capabilities. To be considered within the scope of this effort, the Respondent�s proposed launch vehicle must have development tests demonstrating at least 50% of the flight thrust at the complete full-scale single engine assembly level for all core stage engines of the common launch vehicle configuration being proposed. Launch vehicles that are currently in the conceptual or design stages will not be considered for this specific requirement. Submittal Instructions Please use the Questionnaire document that is provide to answer the RFI questions. All responses should be sent electronically to NASA points of contact identified below NLT 17 November 2026, 3:00PM EST. Any responses submitted through different channels or to a different email may not be considered. When submitting a response, please use the email subject �Response to RFI � NASA MCLS.� Points of Contact Primary Rachel Edwards, Contracting Officer Rachel.t.edwards@nasa.gov Secondary Mary Vaughn, Lead Contracting Officer mary.e.vaughn-1@nasa.gov THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION ONLY. This Sources Sought is being issued for information and planning purposes. It does not constitute a solicitation (Request for Proposal or Request for Quotations) or a promise to issue a solicitation in the future. This Sources Sought does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. Furthermore, the Government is not, at this time, seeking proposals. Respondents to this notice are advised that the Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred by responding to this notice. All costs associated with responding to this notice will be solely at the expense of the responding party. Offerors must submit a bid bond with their proposal. An offeror that does not meet these requirements will be ineligible for award. title: Z2FF-FCI El Reno-Replacement of Housing Unit HVAC Systems
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE FOR MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION, REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP), OR INVITATION FOR BID (IFB). A SYNOPSIS OF PROPOSED CONTRACT ACTION WILL BE POSTED AT A LATER DATE WHICH WILL PROVIDE INSTRUCTIONS FOR BIDDERS TO RESPOND TO THIS OPPORTUNITY.PLEASE DO NOT RESPOND TO THIS NOTICE IF YOU ARE NOT SERIOUSLY INTERESTED AND IF YOU DO NOT PERFORM THIS REQUIREMENT. IT WILL DELAY THE POSTING OF THE SOLICITATION DUE TO FURTHER MARKET RESEARCH THAT WILL BE REQUIRED. The Federal Bureau of Prisons (FBOP) is conducting market research to determine the availability and capability of qualified contractors to perform a design-build construction project at FCI El Reno, Oklahoma. Responses will be used to assist in determining the appropriate acquisition strategy and potential socioeconomic set-aside determination. The Government anticipates issuing a solicitation following completion of market research. Responses must be received no later than 2:00 PM Central Time (CT) on November 17, 2026. Project Location: FCI El Reno, 4205 Highway 66 West, El Reno, OK 73036 NAICS Code: 238220 - Plumbing, Heating, and Air Conditioning Contractors; Small Business Size Standard: $19.0 Million Project Description The Federal Bureau of Prisons anticipates issuing a Firm-Fixed-Price Design-Build Construction Contract for the replacement and modernization of HVAC systems serving five (5) inmate housing facilities at FCI El Reno. The project consists of providing all design, engineering, labor, supervision, materials, equipment, testing, commissioning, and incidental work required to replace aging direct expansion (DX) cooling systems with a modern chilled-water system serving Housing Units A, B, C, D, and the Special Housing Unit (SHU). Work includes removal and disposal of ten (10) existing DX condensing units and associated equipment; design and installation of ten (10) new air-cooled packaged chillers; installation of ten (10) new chilled-water cooling coils; construction of five (5) chiller equipment pads and five (5) temporary chiller landing pads; installation of chilled-water piping systems; electrical distribution modifications and upgrades; installation of five (5) temporary cooling connection stations and five (5) temporary shore-power connection stations; BAS/DDC controls integration; contractor-provided temporary cooling services during phased construction; and all testing, adjusting, balancing (TAB), commissioning, startup, training, and closeout activities. Work will be performed within an occupied, secure federal correctional institution and will require strict compliance with institutional security requirements. Submission Instructions Interested contractors shall complete the attached questionnaire and submit it via email to Jose Dominguez at jdominguez@bop.gov. Responses must be received no later than 2:00 PM Central Time (CT) on November 17, 2026. Vendors are also encouraged to add their name to the Interested Vendors List in SAM.gov.

title: Multi-Mission Commercial Launch Services (MCLS) Request for Information
description: Description NASA�s Commercial Access to Space Program and Launch Services Program Office (LSP) are seeking statements of interest from industry demonstrating the interest, experience, and capability to provide launch services in support of the Multi-Mission Commercial Launch Services (MCLS) requirements identified below. General Project Requirements NASA intends to procure launch services through a full and open competition for at least eight (8) full-mission-assurance launches to the following orbits: Two (2) High C3 Orbit in 2031 Two (2) Lagrange/Lunar Orbit in 2030 Three (3) Sun Synchronous Orbit (SSO) in 2030 (2 mission) and 2031 (1 mission) One (1) Low Earth Orbit (LEO) in 2030 These missions will require full NASA insight and full mission assurance; however, they will not require a completed first flight prior to proposal receipt. Full mission assurance is described as a Contractor providing NASA an adequate level of insight into and/or approval of certain Contractor tasks and milestones in order to ensure all reasonable steps have been taken that result in the highest probability of mission success. These requirements are subject to change. Request for Information Goals and Objectives The goal of this RFI is to improve both NASA's understanding of industry capabilities and the industry's understanding of NASA's needs by collecting industry feedback on the planned procurement process and evaluation strategy for the MCLS acquisition. This information will help LSP understand how to best structure the upcoming solicitation and evaluation criteria to align with industry�s best practices and maximize competition. Please complete the attached questionnaire detailing your perspectives on the most effective procurement approach. Industry Day: NASA LSP intends to host a virtual forum with industry (i.e., �Industry Day�) on the 12th and 13th of November 2026 to engage in open discussion and dialogue to answer questions interested parties may have regarding the NASA�s contemplated MCLS acquisition strategy. The objective of this event is to receive industry�s feedback on the MCLS acquisition strategy and provide industry with additional details about the MCLS acquisition. Additionally, if there are any procurement topics you recommend LSP specifically address at Industry Day, please let us know by 10 November 2026. Finally, please indicate if you would like to discuss any topic(s) individually. Immediately following Industry Day, LSP will offer sixty (60)-minute timeslots for one-on-one meetings with each interested party. Timing of these one-on-one meetings is tentative and will depend on the number of RSVPs received, timing of the Industry Day, etc. Those who wish to attend are encouraged to RSVP to the virtual Industry Day and one-on-one meetings as soon as possible, but no later than 9 November 2026, 3:00PM EST. The purpose of this RFI and upcoming Industry Day is to conduct market research for currently available launch capabilities. To be considered within the scope of this effort, the Respondent�s proposed launch vehicle must have development tests demonstrating at least 50% of the flight thrust at the complete full-scale single engine assembly level for all core stage engines of the common launch vehicle configuration being proposed. Launch vehicles that are currently in the conceptual or design stages will not be considered for this specific requirement. Submittal Instructions Please use the Questionnaire document that is provide to answer the RFI questions. All responses should be sent electronically to NASA points of contact identified below NLT 17 November 2026, 3:00PM EST. Any responses submitted through different channels or to a different email may not be considered. When submitting a response, please use the email subject �Response to RFI � NASA MCLS.� Points of Contact Primary Rachel Edwards, Contracting Officer Rachel.t.edwards@nasa.gov Secondary Mary Vaughn, Lead Contracting Officer mary.e.vaughn-1@nasa.gov THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION ONLY. This Sources Sought is being issued for information and planning purposes. It does not constitute a solicitation (Request for Proposal or Request for Quotations) or a promise to issue a solicitation in the future. This Sources Sought does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. Furthermore, the Government is not, at this time, seeking proposals. Respondents to this notice are advised that the Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred by responding to this notice. All costs associated with responding to this notice will be solely at the expense of the responding party. Intellectual or other privileged information contained in responses to this Sources Sought will not be distributed outside of NASA or United States Government employees from other Government agencies. Amendment 1 (11/9/2026) Please note that in accordance with the Commercial Space Act of 1998 (Title 51 U.S.C. � 50131), the U.S. Government is required to acquire space transportation services from United States commercial providers. Therefore, eligibility to submit responses to this Request for Information and participate in the associated Industry Day is restricted to domestic (U.S.) commercial entities.

title: Authentication Services for FISMA Support
description: INTRODUCTION AND BACKGROUND This is a Sources Sought Notice (SSN) issued by the Treasury Common Services Center (TCSC), Acquisition Services, on behalf of the Bureau of the Fiscal Service (Fiscal Service), Identity, Credentialing & Access Management (ICAM) Division. The purpose of this notice is to obtain industry information and identify 8(a) sources that are both capable of and interested in providing commercial Engineer and Project Management Services for the execution of Authentication Services for Federal Information Security Modernization Action (FISMA) Support as described herein. This information is being sought for acquisition planning purposes only. SCOPE AND OBJECTIVES Fiscal Services is seeking to identify Contractors who can provide highly skilled and technical contractual support for Information System Security Officer (ISSO) duties and audit liaison for the Authentication Services General Support System (AS GSS). Subject Matter Expert (SME) Contractor support shall include assistance in the development, maintenance, and oversight of the Authentication Services FISMA system, including Security Controls, Continuity of Operations, plans, and related exercises surrounding access to Fiscal Service IT resources. Contractor resources also support the management and response to user access issues and problems within the ICAM Division for the AS GSS system and its sub-components. The Contractor shall perform all Authentication Services; FISMA related tasks generally assigned to an Information System Security Officer and all related Identity, Credentialing, and Access Management Security audit tasks include: Provide, monitor, and manage the AS GSS as an Information System Security Officer (ISSO). This includes the creation, management, and maintenance of all FISMA lifecycle tasks, deliverables, and continuous monitoring indicator tasks within the Government, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) tool. Review, develop and maintain documentation of ICAM processes, procedures, and operations pertaining to providing and managing user access to Fiscal Service IT Resources via the AS GSS. Provide expert guidance, training, and assistance with the closure of issues discovered during Vulnerability Scanning. Perform Audit Liaison activities for the various Audits and Assessments that are conducted against Authentication Services and Central Authentication and Identity Assurance (CAIA) fronted applications. This includes the Schedule of the Federal Debt, Consolidated Financial Statement, Office of Inspector General (OIG) and Government Accountability Office (GAO) audits. Support and Maintain ICAM Organization and Identity Administration functions: ICAM Operations and Help Desk Respond to ICAM program and daily operational needs Maintain and monitor the PKI, LDAP, SSO, Splunk, Vault and CAIA service for ICAM Liaison with the AS application and service users Liaison with other FS and FRB ISSO�s and System Owners Authentication Services Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Support User Provisioning Administration, reconciliation and reporting: Create and maintain Authentication Services in-boundary and service user Policies, Standards and Procedures. Review and act upon issues seen on the Authentication Services transaction Logs via Enterprise Log Management (Splunk). Manage and review access reconciliation and recertification policies, standards and procedures for all aspects of the AS GSS. The Contractor shall participate with ongoing cloud migration initiatives, assisting with all access and security controls to ensure optimal security posture and compliance with National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), Treasury and Fiscal Service IT Security Standards and Business Line Security Requirements (BLSRs). The Contractor shall provide training for personnel on IT related subjects centering on NIST regulatory requirements. Conduct the ICAM Technical Support (DTS) Contract Status Meeting Develop ICAM Technical Support (DTS) Contract Status Report Perform Fiscal Service Authentication Services FISMA ISSO Duties and Reporting Inventory Record of Government Furnished Property

title: Public Accountant Contract Audits (PACA) Installation Audits (USAFE region)
description: The Air Force Services Center (AFSVC), headquartered at Joint Base San Antonio- Lackland, Texas, delivers Services programs and activities to build and sustain ready and resilient Airmen, Guardians and families. Air Force Services Center supports the bases, major commands and air staff by providing technical assistance, new initiatives, developing programs and procedures and managing central support functions. Air Force Services Center ensures successful operation of essential food, fitness, childcare, lodging and recreation opportunities for military members and their families. The Center�s responsibilities include preparing responses to high-level inquiries, providing technical assistance to the field and developing new programs that support major command and installation activities. The Financial Management Directorate (VF) manages the Nonappropriated Fund Public Accountant Contract Audit program centrally which supports a worldwide mission providing an oversight of internal controls, cash management and financial information to installations at the enterprise level. Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) installations provide support services and activities for military personnel, families and authorized patrons. Proper management and accountability of Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) resources are critical to ensuring continued service delivery and the protection of government interests. Regular audits are required to evaluate the financial status, internal controls, and operational effectiveness of Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) operations. The Air Force Services Center Financial Management, Strategic Policy & Financial Operations, AFSVC/VFSF manages and administers audit oversight to Central Funds and the Public Accountant Contract Audit (PACA) Program to ensure compliance with annual audit requirements of financial statements audits of the NAFIs and that adequate audit coverage is provided Air Force wide for the Nonappropriated Fund Instrumentalities (NAFIs) Services activities. The Contractor shall conduct comprehensive audits of the financial statements, transactions, internal controls, and performance of Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) installations and activities. AFSVC is seeking to contract an audit firm for a 5-year period, structured with a Base Year and four (4) subsequent Option Years. AFSVC intends to issue initial Base Year task orders requiring dual-year financial statement audits encompassing two distinct historical fiscal years as designated in the individual task orders (e.g., FY24 and FY25). While financial statement audits will examine specific, historical fiscal years, performance audits will be conducted on an as-needed basis determined by an annual risk assessment, with the specific scope defined in individual task orders. All interested quoters are invited to submit questions by 2:00PM, CST, Monday, 9 November 2026. Submit all quotes no later than (NLT) 2:00PM, CST, Tuesdsy, 17 Nov 2026 via email to valerie.baltimore@us.af.mil and whitney.ward.1@us.af.mil. The RFQ closes at 2:00PM, CST, Tuesday, 17 Nov 2026.

title: NIH Scientific & Technical Expertise & Acquisition Management (STEAM)
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE NIH SCIENTIFIC & TECHNICAL EXPERTISE ACQUISITION & MANAGEMENT (STEAM) Sources Sought Reference Number: 75N98027R00012 Proposed NAICS Code and Size Standard: 541990 � All Other Professional, Scientific and Technical Services; $19.5 million in average annual receipts Sources Sought Notice Information Introduction This is a Small Business Sources Sought notice. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding: (1) the availability and capability of qualified small business sources; (2) their small business and applicable socioeconomic status, including HUBZone, service-disabled veteran-owned, veteran-owned, 8(a), woman-owned, and small disadvantaged business status; and (3) their size classification relative to the proposed North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code. Responses will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method, including whether a full or partial small business set-aside is appropriate. Interested small businesses may respond for Task Area A (Professional Services), Task Area B (Highly Specialized Scientific Services), or both. Respondents should identify their ability to perform as a prime contractor, joint venture, or subcontracting team, distinguish their own capability from that of team members, and identify limitations within each task area addressed. NIH will assess capability separately for each area. Capability in both areas is not required to respond. The Government has not made a final set-aside determination. Background The National Institutes of Health (NIH) conducts and supports biomedical and behavioral research to advance scientific knowledge and improve health. NIH requires professional, scientific, and technical contractor support for current and emerging research priorities, ongoing research activities, and related program operations. Changes in research programs and scientific methods create a continuing need for flexible service delivery and specialized expertise. Scientific & Technical Expertise Acquisition & Management (STEAM) will acquire contractor-provided services and expertise to accomplish varied project-based requirements across NIH. Individual task orders will define project objectives, tasks, deliverables or milestones, performance periods, required expertise, and resource needs. Contractors must furnish and manage the resources needed to perform multiple concurrent projects at substantial volume and adjust those resources as authorized project requirements change. NIH anticipates using cost-reimbursement contracting approximately 20 percent of the time. The actual mix will depend on individual requirements. Firms should describe their experience and ability to support this component, including any preparation needed. Existing cost-reimbursement capability or a prior Government accounting-system approval is not a mandatory condition of responding to this notice. Applicable requirements, including accounting-system adequacy, would need to be satisfied before award of a cost-reimbursement order. Purpose and Objectives The purpose of STEAM is to provide professional, scientific, and technical support for NIH research and related activities. Support includes basic, translational, and clinical research; vaccine research; general and specialized laboratory research; veterinary and animal research support; bioinformatics; computational biology; and related professional and technical services. The contractor will furnish and manage qualified resources to accomplish each statement of work (SOW), including responsibility for recruiting, verifying qualifications, retaining its personnel, and maintaining continuity of performance. Services will be furnished under individual funded, project-based task orders. The contractor will furnish resources, including personnel with expertise corresponding to the applicable labor categories, to accomplish the SOW and deliver the required project outcomes and milestones. The contractor will retain responsibility for employing, supervising, and managing its personnel. Services will not include inherently governmental functions or unauthorized personal services. Each task order will identify the applicable task area, project scope, qualifications, location, performance schedule, and security and safety requirements. Project Requirements Services may involve expertise in microbiology, molecular biology, biochemistry, infectious diseases, immunology, clinical research, bioinformatics, genomic sequencing, proteomics, image analysis, computational and systems biology, and scientific data analysis. Related requirements may include clinical trials support, laboratory operations, veterinary services, program management, and other professional or technical support within the authorized scope. Qualifications range from positions without a degree requirement to licensed practitioners and highly specialized doctoral-level professionals. The contractor must be able to furnish qualified resources within the task area or areas addressed and manage a substantial volume of concurrent project requirements. Primary anticipated locations include Bethesda and Rockville, Maryland; other locations in the Washington, DC metropolitan area; and Hamilton, Montana. Other domestic locations, overseas support, travel, or remote work may be authorized by individual orders. NIH-wide demand for task orders and contractor support fluctuates across projects, locations, and time. This notice does not provide a fixed annual volume estimate or guarantee a minimum workload. Routine task orders will establish mobilization, onboarding, and performance start schedules. Under certain circumstances, an urgent or unforeseen NIH need may require the contractor to begin authorized performance within 48 hours. For an expedited request, NIH will identify the applicable timeframe and the event from which it is measured. Respondents should describe their ability to accommodate these requests, identify the categories and locations they could support, and explain any limitations or prerequisites. Contractors must ensure that their personnel have the qualifications and relevant experience required for the assigned work and complete applicable training, competency verification, occupational health requirements, and facility-specific access approvals before beginning restricted work. For assignments involving regulated select agents or toxins, applicable individual access approvals, security risk assessments, and required training must be completed before access. Prior experience at another laboratory does not establish authorization at the receiving NIH facility. An expedited task-order request does not waive these prerequisites. The following 156 labor-category families are organized into two task areas. Each family appears once. Categories encompass applicable levels and specialties; task orders will specify required duties and qualifications. Numbered levels are not automatically equivalent to Junior, Mid-Level, or Senior designations. The task-area structure supports market research and does not establish the final award structure. Task Area A � Professional Services This area covers general professional, management, administrative, business, IT, and technical support for NIH projects, including project coordination, financial analysis, enterprise systems, and related operational services. Scientific versions of otherwise general roles are assigned to Task Area B.
